blocks.html: In criminal matters, before the judge can come to condemnation, two things principally must appear to him. The first, that the crime in question has truly been committed and perpetrated a. The second, that the person whom one wishes to punish is the one who committed the offence, or is otherwise culpable of the deed.

notes.citation: Digest 29.5 (De senatus consulto Silaniano et Claudiano: quorum testamenta ne aperiantur), l. 1, § Item illud (D. 29.5.1, Ulpian; paragraph not identified); Code 3.26 (Ubi causae fiscales vel divinae domus hominumque eius agantur), l. 1 (C. 3.26.1)
notes.original: l. j. P. item illud. D. ad Silania l. j. C. vbi cauſ. fiſcæ.
notes.gloss: Under the Silanian decree the inquiry into the household proceeds only when it is first established that the master was killed, which is Coras's first head: that the crime was in fact committed. The bearing of the Code text could not be verified. The P. stands for the paragraph sign.

notes.citation: Code 9.47 (De poenis), l. Sancimus (C. 9.47.22, Arcadius and Honorius)
notes.gloss: Sancimus ibi esse poenam, ubi et noxa est: "We ordain that the punishment be there where the guilt is"; kinsmen, acquaintances and familiars are not to be touched by it.
